en.headline: Think tank says more than a quarter of students want sports careers
en.dek: Our Hong Kong Foundation surveyed about 1,100 secondary pupils and called for dual-track school guidelines and clearer entry routes into the industry.
body: Our Hong Kong Foundation said a survey of secondary students found that more than a quarter wanted to work in the sports industry, but many did not know how to enter it or what jobs existed beyond playing and coaching.

Researchers collected 1,098 valid questionnaires from more than 40 schools between February and March. About 28 per cent of respondents said they intended to join the sports sector. Fifty-six per cent did not know the industry also includes roles such as sports psychologists and data analysts. Nearly half were unclear about entry pathways, and nearly 30 per cent cited a lack of practical opportunities.

The foundation said demand for sports talent would rise as more major events come to Hong Kong. It recommended that the government draw up dual-track development guidelines for secondary schools, improve career-planning websites with job and internship information, and raise the weighting of youth participation in the scoring of M-brand events.
The think tank also said the authorities could consider making permanent the funding now given to universities under the SALSA scheme to support elite athletes in admissions.

zh.headline: 團結香港基金：逾四分一中學生有意投身體育行業
zh.dek: 基金會訪問約1,100名中學生，指近半人不清楚入行途徑，建議為全港中學編制雙軌發展指引。
body: 團結香港基金公布一項中學生調查，指超過四分一受訪者有意日後投身體育行業，但不少人並不清楚入行途徑，亦不知道行業除運動員和教練外還有其他職位。
研究團隊今年2至3月向40多間中學發出問卷，收回1,098份有效回覆。約28%受訪者表示有意加入體育行業；56%不知道行業亦包括運動心理學家、數據分析員等崗位。近半數不清楚入行途徑，近三成認為缺乏實踐機會。
基金會表示，隨著更多體育盛事落戶香港，運動醫療、營養及體育軟件開發等人才需求會上升。團隊建議政府為全港中學編制「雙軌發展指引」，優化生涯規劃資訊網站，並在「M」品牌活動評分中提高青少年參與元素的比重。
基金會又建議，當局可考慮將現時向大學提供、用以支援精英運動員入學的「SALSA計劃」資助恆常化。
